canonical_title: Clarion: Data Warehouse and Business Intelligence for Campus Analytics
abstract: In a world that is driven by data, every business across all sectors are looking to gain an edge over their competitors using every data they have and that they might obtain. University and educational industry are no exceptions. The problems, however, lie in fragments of data sources inside the organization. In addition to fragmentation of data, is the lack of tools to come up with meaningful insights. At first, out goal is to research and see what value can existing data bring us. We took a change to interview the university registrar. He told us of his vision, what he wants to see, what he wants to know and what is available. From there, we drafted our project and to try to answer and deliver the university registrar goals; A tool that can use existing data to answers business questions around the university. Hence, our project Clarion. Our first task in the development of Clarion is to understand what we have. So we spent the first couple of weeks to study data and its sources. We have identified three available sources being Keystone; university registrar's student information system, AU Spark; a student information mobile application, and data from the university registrar itself. Getting to understand available data as well as its format, we started designing our project. We decided to create the Clarion; a bundle of data warehouse and business dashboards for Assumption University of Thailand. Clarion is a data warehouse designed for Assumption University of Thailand. Merging many data sources into one single meaningful platform consisting of Power BI report and OLAP cube. In Power BI, we have prepared dashboards with different aspects of university data with built-in filters for users. They can play around and manipulate queries via a neatly designed interface that is provided by Power BI. OLAP cube, on the other hand, is a blank canvas of strategically cleaned data. Users can freely explore data themselves by dragging and dropping dimensions on to the screen to come up with insights or to answers any business questions they might have.

canonical_title: Flying Basket: A Mobile App for Indian Grocery Online Shopping
aliases: Mobile Application for Online Grocery Shopping
advisor: Asst. Prof. Dr. Anilkumar Kothalil Gopalakrishnan
committee: Asst. Prof. Dr. Dobri Atanassov Batovski
abstract: This project focuses on ordering Indian grocery items online. Currently it is a mobile application for android users that is fully responsive. The grocery store owners can add items that can be listed for sale for the customers that are the users of the application. On the same hand the application is a user friendly and easy to use system where the user can add the items to their carts and simply place order via the mobile application. Every data is stored on the cloud. This application is the only application in Bangkok that focuses on the online service of delivering Indian grocery items. It reduces the hassle of the people who go to shop for these products. This application will allow you to sit at your home and order the products and they will be delivered to your doorstep fresh. We are anticipating that this application would be useful to the Indian community in Bangkok.

abstract: Opinion mining tools help analysts check whether products get good reviews, but surveys are expensive, slow to collect, and often out of date. This project develops a standalone system that classifies tweets from Twitter as fact or opinion and as positive or negative sentiment, focused on the movie domain. Around 30,000 movie related tweets were retrieved with the Twitter API, manually labelled, and preprocessed by removing URLs, mentions, hashtags, non alphabetic characters and stop words, and by Snowball stemming. Three classification algorithms, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, and k Nearest Neighbors, were compared in Weka using accuracy, precision, recall, and F measure with 10 fold cross validation. Naive Bayes performed best and was implemented in the final system, which lets the user train, evaluate, search Twitter, and test single sentences.

abstract: In Thai housing villages the juristic person must announce news, invoice maintenance fees, and track parcels for residents, while residents often miss notifications and paper records are hard to maintain. This project develops PNC, a web application that gathers maintenance fee payment, parcel management, and circular letter announcement in one system. It was built with the MERN stack, which combines MongoDB, Express JS, React JS with Redux, and Node JS, using the Agile methodology. The system records resident information to calculate maintenance fees automatically, notifies residents of invoices and arriving parcels, and lets the juristic person announce news and confirm payment evidence uploaded by residents. The current version helps the juristic person collect maintenance fees, and a future version aims to cover water and electricity bill payments.

abstract: This project is aimed for keeping records of a kid from newborn infants to around 18 years is common everywhere around the world. This application is being developed to help the mothers of children to keep track of the medical and physical record of their child. This is a mobile-based application. The users can record the body development, vaccination, allergies of their kids. Moreover, they can also record notes regarding their kids. It also provides notification to remind the user of the time for their child to take vaccination. This can be very helpful to the users who are busy with their work and want to keep track of their child medical record and physical record. Finally, this system is anticipated to be very useful to the users who want to record everything in their child's life.
